title: Article 220 — Restriction on practice after being a permanent Judge

content.overview: Article 220 provides that no person who, after the commencement of the Constitution, has held office as a permanent Judge of a High Court shall plead or act in any court or before any authority in India except the Supreme Court and the other High Courts.
content.glance: Permanent HC Judge (post-commencement) cannot plead or act in any court/authority in India except the Supreme Court and other High Courts.
content.study:
Article 220 restricts post-retirement practice of permanent High Court Judges to the Supreme Court and other High Courts only — not in the High Court where they served as permanent Judge, nor in subordinate courts or other authorities in India.

Examination: permanent Judge; post-commencement; exception for SC and other HCs only.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: No person who has held office as a permanent Judge of a High Court after commencement shall plead or act in any court or before any authority in India except the Supreme Court and the other High Courts.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What restriction does Article 220 impose on permanent High Court Judges?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 220, no person who, after the commencement of the Constitution, has held office as a permanent Judge of a High Court shall plead or act in any court or before any authority in India except the Supreme Court and the other High Courts.

examTips: Permanent HC Judge: practice only in SC and other HCs.

keyTakeaways: Art 220: restriction on practice after permanent HC Judgeship.
